# Dream Analysis and Interpretation

The dream is a little hidden door in the innermost and most secret recesses of the soul, opening into that cosmic night which was psyche long before there was any ego-consciousness, and which will remain psyche no matter how far our ego-consciousness may extend. Dreams are the natural reaction of the self-regulating psychic system, compensating the one-sidedness of conscious attitudes.

Dream interpretation requires that we abandon all preconceived notions and let the dream speak for itself. The manifest content of a dream is not a mask for its latent meaning; the dream is exactly what it appears to be, a symbolic expression of the unconscious situation. Every dream is a message from the unconscious to the conscious mind, using the language of symbols and images rather than concepts.

In dream analysis, the method of amplification is essential. Rather than reducing dream images to simple drives or wishes, we amplify them by collecting all the associations, mythological parallels, and archetypal images that cluster around a given symbol. Dreams employ symbols because they attempt to express something for which no verbal concept yet exists. The symbols in dreams are not signs with fixed meanings but living images that point beyond themselves.

Recurring dreams deserve special attention, for they indicate that the dreaming psyche is struggling with a particular problem that consciousness has failed to resolve. The series of dreams over time often reveals a narrative of psychological development — an individuation process unfolding in the language of the night. Dream interpretation is not an art to be learned from books but requires long practice and intimate knowledge of the dreamer's situation.
